engines.name: Electric, 77.4 kWh Long Range (RWD or AWD)
Electric, 84 kWh Long Range (RWD, AWD or XRT)

issues.t: Charging unit (ICCU) failure and loss of drive power (recall)
issues.sym: A '12V battery low' or 'Check EV system' warning, charging that stops or won't start, a loud pop from under the car, then reduced power or the car shutting down while driving.
issues.why: The Integrated Charging Control Unit (ICCU) charges both the big battery and the small 12-volt battery. It can be damaged by a current surge and stop charging the 12-volt battery, and when that battery runs down the car loses drive power.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for recall 24V-868 (which replaced 24V-204). Dealers update the ICCU software and replace the ICCU and its fuse if needed, for free. If the warning shows while driving, pull over safely as soon as you can.

issues.t: Battery cells can have a fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem. The concern is a battery fire while parked or driving.
issues.why: Some high-voltage battery cells may have been built with misaligned electrodes, which can cause an internal short and a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 26V-432. Until it is fixed, park outside and away from buildings and limit charging to 80%. Dealers will replace the high-voltage battery assembly free.

issues.t: Battery bus bar bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Possible warning lights or the car going into a reduced-power fail-safe mode. In the worst case, arcing inside the battery pack could start a fire.
issues.why: Bolts holding the high-voltage bus bars (the metal straps that join battery modules) may not have been tightened enough at the factory. Only a small number of Georgia-built cars are affected.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 25V-482 and 26V-068. Dealers inspect the bolts and tighten them for free.

issues.t: 'Power is limited' warning or whine from the rear motor
issues.sym: A turtle symbol and 'Power is limited' message, or a whining noise from the rear when speeding up or slowing below about 25 mph.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin to inspect the electric oil pump in the drive unit when this warning appears. One 2023 owner reports a failed cooling pump that damaged the rear motor, which was replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Have a Hyundai dealer read the codes (such as P0A2F) and check bulletin 24-EV-003H. The drive motor is covered by Hyundai's EV warranty, so don't put this off.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden clunk and loss of drive power, or the car rolling when in Park without the parking brake set.
issues.why: Some rear inner driveshafts may not have been heat-treated correctly and can break under load.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-065. Dealers replace the affected driveshafts for free. Use the electric parking brake whenever you park until it is done.

issues.t: Car can roll away after being put in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car moves after you shift into Park and get out.
issues.why: A software error in the shifter control unit could release the parking mechanism.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-324. Dealers update the software for free. Always set the electric parking brake until it is done.

issues.t: Rear suspension bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the car feeling loose or pulling, or a stability control warning.
issues.why: Fasteners in the rear suspension, including the alignment adjusting bolts, may not have been tightened properly at the factory and can loosen or come out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 26V-314 and 25V-605. Dealers inspect and tighten or replace the bolts for free.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractors may not be secured (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving; a seat belt might not hold properly in a crash.
issues.why: The driver and front passenger seat belt retractors may not have been fastened securely to the body.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-797. Dealers inspect and properly secure the retractors for free.

issues.t: Rear side airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A wiring harness under the rear floor may have an open circuit, so the rear side airbag might not deploy in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-064 and have the dealer repair the harness for free.

issues.t: Right headlight may be aimed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The right headlight shines too high or too low at night.
issues.why: The right headlight may carry an incorrect aiming label, so it could be aimed incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-373. Dealers check and re-aim the headlight for free.

issues.t: Ioniq 5 N brake software fault (recall)
issues.sym: Braking may not respond as expected when braking with the left foot or using the N e-shift feature.
issues.why: A software defect in the integrated electronic brake and vehicle control units on the Ioniq 5 N.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 25V-065 and 25V-235. Dealers update the software for free.

issues.t: Instrument display may not show speed or warnings (recall)
issues.sym: The digital gauge display may not show speed or warning lights under certain conditions.
issues.why: A problem with the instrument cluster software across several Hyundai models.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for recall 26V-047. Dealers update or replace the cluster for free.

issues.t: 12-volt battery goes flat and the car won't wake up
issues.sym: A '12V battery low' message, or you press start and nothing happens. It often follows the car sitting for days or after fast charging.
issues.why: All the car's computers run off a small 12-volt battery, separate from the main pack. A weak battery, a software issue, or an ICCU that isn't charging it can let it run down.
issues.next: Jump-start from the 12-volt terminals under the hood or use the reset button if your car has one. If it keeps happening, have the dealer test the battery and ICCU and load the latest software.

issues.t: Heater or A/C stops working
issues.sym: No heat or no cooling from the vents, sometimes on a nearly new car.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for heater and A/C failures with specific climate system fault codes on early Ioniq 5s.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the climate codes and follow bulletin 23-HA-002H. It is covered by warranty.

issues.t: Charging port caps missing or damaged
issues.sym: A charging plug that doesn't seat well or a fast charger that won't start a session.
issues.why: Small insulation caps inside the charging port help the plug line up and fit. Hyundai found they can be missing or damaged.
issues.next: Look inside the port for missing or broken caps and ask the dealer to check under bulletin 23-EV-006H.

issues.t: Jerky or hesitant response in Eco mode (AWD)
issues.sym: On all-wheel-drive models in Eco mode, the car hesitates, surges or feels unsmooth when you press or lift off the pedal.
issues.why: The vehicle control unit software handling the front motor in Eco mode. Hyundai released a software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the software update in bulletin 23-EV-002H.

issues.t: Noise from the steering column when turning
issues.sym: A knock, click or grinding noise when turning the steering wheel.
issues.why: Hyundai found a worn bearing on the worm shaft in the electric power steering column.
issues.next: Have the dealer check under bulletins 22-ST-005H and 22-ST-008H; the bearing is replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Rattle from the tailgate
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from the rear hatch over bumps.
issues.why: The tailgate can move slightly against its latch. Hyundai's fix adds washer pads and adjusts the striker.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to fix it under bulletin 23-BD-006H.

issues.t: Active air flap warning
issues.sym: An active air flap warning on the dash while driving.
issues.why: The motor that opens and closes the grille air flaps can fail. Hyundai's fix is a new actuator.
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the actuator under bulletin 23-01-075H.

issues.t: Driver's power seat stops moving
issues.sym: The power controls for the driver's seat stop working.
issues.why: A wiring harness under the seat can get pinched or rubbed by the seat track.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and reroute or repair the harness under bulletin 23-01-066H.

issues.t: Touch screen freezes or radio app crashes
issues.sym: The center screen freezes or reboots, the radio app crashes, phone projection drops, or a false 'Uneven road ahead' message appears.
issues.why: Software bugs in the head unit. Hyundai has released several updates.
issues.next: Install the latest navigation and head unit software at a dealer or from Hyundai's update site.
